Learning to Filter: Siamese Relation Network for Robust Tracking
Siyuan Cheng1,2, Bineng Zhong1*, Guorong Li3, Xin Liu4, Zhenjun Tang1, Xianxian Li1*, Jing Wang2
1Guangxi Key Lab of Multi-Source Information Mining & Security,
Guangxi Normal University, Guilin 541004, China
2Department of Computer Science and Technology, Huaqiao University, China
3School of Computer Science and Technology, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, China,
4Seetatech Technology, Beijing, China
siyuancheng@stu.hqu.edu.cn, bnzhong@gxnu.edu.cn, liguorong@ucas.ac.cn
xin.liu@seetatech.com, rrji@xmu.edu.cn, tangzj230@163.com,
lixx@gxnu.edu.cn, wroaring@hqu.edu.cn
Abstract
Despite the great success of Siamese-based trackers,
their performance under complicated scenarios is still not
satisfying, especially when there are distractors. To this
end, we propose a novel Siamese relation network, which
introduces two efﬁcient modules, i.e. Relation Detector
(RD) and Reﬁnement Module (RM). RD performs in a meta-
learning way to obtain a learning ability to ﬁlter the dis-
tractors from the background while RM aims to effectively
integrate the proposed RD into the Siamese framework to
generate accurate tracking result. Moreover, to further im-
prove the discriminability and robustness of the tracker, we
introduce a contrastive training strategy that attempts not
only to learn matching the same target but also to learn
how to distinguish the different objects.
Therefore, our
tracker can achieve accurate tracking results when fac-
ing background clutters, fast motion, and occlusion. Ex-
perimental results on ﬁve popular benchmarks, including
VOT2018, VOT2019, OTB100, LaSOT, and UAV123, show
that the proposed method is effective and can achieve state-
of-the-art results. The code will be available at https:
//github.com/hqucv/siamrn
